chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

'There is no day that comes to the son of Adam except that that day says to him: O son of Adam! I am a new day, and I am a witness upon you, so speak good in me and do good in me, and I shall testify for you with it on the Day of Judgment, for you will not see me after it ever.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so that whenever Ali (peace be upon him) became evening, he would say: Welcome to the new night and the recording witness, write by the Name of Allah.' Then he would mention (do dhikr of) Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: How does the concept of time serve as a witness in Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of the personification of time as a divine witness, urging believers to maximize their spiritual capital in each fleeting day. It connects this ethical imperative to the prophetic tradition of Imam Ali (peace be upon him), who ritualized the transition of time by greeting the evening as a 'new night' and 'recording witness,' thereby embedding mindfulness of the Hereafter into daily routine. This practice underscores the importance of consistent dhikr and intentional action as preparation for the ultimate accountability.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from the days which comes to the son of Adam<sup>as</sup> except, that day would say: ‘O son of Adam<sup>as</sup>! I am a new day, and I am a witness upon you, therefore speak good during me, and do good deeds during me, I shall testify with it on the Day of Judgment, for you will not be seeing me (again) afterwards, ever”’.

Heasws said: ‘And it was so that whenever it was evening, Aliasws was saying: ‘Welcome to the new night and the recording witnesses who both write by the Name of Allahazwj’. Then heasws would mention (do Zikr of) Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Each coming day says to the sons of Adam, ‘O son of Adam, I am a new day and a witness over you. Say good in me and do good deeds; I will testify for or against you on the Day of Judgment. You will never see me thereafter.’

The Imam said that Ali (a.s.) in the evening would say, ‘Welcome to the new night, and witnessing ascribe. Both of you write down in the name of Allah.’ Then he would speak of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’”
